text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN FINANCIAL REVIEW

Pacific Dunlop managing director Rod Chadwick announced last night the group's Telectronics has been sold to rival medical equipment manufacturer St Jude Medical Inc for A$170 million. PacDun shareholders have watched more than A$3 billion of value evaporate following the discovery of some faulty pacemaker leads made by Telectronics which resulted in 32 people injured and six deaths. Page 1.

Foxtel partners, Rupert Murdoch's News Corp and Telstra, are expected to commence legal action in the Federal Court within days, using the Trade Practices Act to argue that the alliance between Kerry Packer's Optus Vision and Australis Media is likely to lessen competition in pay-TV and related markets such as movies and sports programming. Page 1.

Coles Myer Ltd director Nick Greiner yesterday indicated that legal action over the Australian Securities Commission's release of transcripts dealing with the Yannon transaction would be settled out of court. However, Greiner failed to point out if he was referring to the legal action by fellow Coles Myer director Solomon Lew or action taken by Premier Investments' Harry Cooper and Monica Vinson. Page 5.

Marking the departure of the seventh senior executive from trans-Tasman brewer Lion Nathan Ltd in the past year, former South African Breweries executive Tony van Kralingen has resigned as the managing director of Lion's Australian operations after only two months. Page 25.

Normandy Mining Ltd executive chairman Robert Champion de Crespigny told shareholders at yesterday's annual meeting that, as part of a plan to raise awareness of the newly merged gold group and encourage a rerating of its stock price, the company could lit in both Toronto and New York and would send group general manager in charge of corporate, Colin Jackson, to North America to pave the way for a listing. Page 25.

South Australian-based softwood timber group Auspine Ltd yesterday forecast a A$5 million first half trading loss and the possibility of asset writedowns because of stagnant housing construction and a slump in woodchip prices. Auspine also announced the ppointment of Sydney merchant banker Geoff Hill as chairman and Adelaide lawyer Paul Teisseire as an independent director. Page 27.
THE AUSTRALIAN

Although yesterday's release of September quarter consumer price index data increased the chances of a pre-Christmas interest rate cut - the CPI rose 0.3 per cent, giving a rate for the year to September of 2.1 per cent - economists say today's average wekly earnings data for the August quarter will be crucial to the Reserve Bank's monetary policy deliberations. Page 23.

Normandy Mining Ltd investor relations head, Colin Jackson, will go to the US in mid-November for a three-month tour of institutional investors in a bid to win the stock market rerating promised at the time of Normandy's A$4 billion merger in August. Jackson will also decide on which North American stock exchange the company will list. Page 23.

Pacific Dunlop Ltd has sold its troubled Telectronics Pacing Systems subsidiary to US-based medical devices group St Jude Medical Inc for A$170 million, but PacDun still faces the threat of multi-million-dollar legal action over faulty heart pacemaker leas manufactured by Telectronics. Page 23.

Amid Australian Stock Exchange concerns that BHP may have breached the Corporations Law, rival petroleum companies claim BHP justifiably withheld disclosure of its 11,790 barrels-a-day Buffalo 1 oil strike until the closure of tender offers for two nearby tenements in Indonesian waters, SABO and RABE, even though the discovery may have affected the value of the tenements. Page 23.

As Standard & Poor's declared it had cut Australian National Industries Ltd's credit rating from BBB to BBB-, Bankers Trust revealed itself as a major buyer of ANI shares, purchasing 8.5 million shares on market last Thursday to take its ANI voting stake rom 12.15 per cent to 13.22 per cent. Page 25.

As part of a A$300 million strategy to increase exports of specialty chemicals to Asian markets, plastics and chemicals giant ICI Australia Ltd will spend A$22 million to improve productivity at is surfactants plant at Botany in New South Wales by improvig existing facilities and establishing a centralised packaging facility. Page 25.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

Australia's inflation numbers were in line with expectations yesterday, as the underlying inflation rate fell to 2.4 per cent from 3.1 per cent, well within the Reserve Bank's two to three per cent target band. However, today's wages figures will be the key to any pre-Christmas interest rate cut. Page 25.

In reference to Coles Myer and its former chairman and current director Solomon Lew, Coles director Nick Greiner told the 1996 CPA Victorian Congress in Melbourne yesterday that it was probably desirable to disallow related party transactions. Greiner said corporate governance should not be seen as the "holy grail" but he recommended companies stick to a set of guidelines. Page 25.

Australia's biggest fund manager, AMP Society, is leading a flight of capital into higher-growth foreign markets because of the inability to achieve above average investment returns from Australian financial markets. UK consulting group CAMRA forecasts global investments by Australian superannuation funds alone will rise from A$40.5 billion to A$100 billion by 2001. Page 25.

Pacific Dunlop has sold its troubled Telectronics pacemaker business to US-based group St Jude Medical for A$170 million. However, any liabilities arising from two pending class actions in North America associated with faulty pacemaker leads will stay with Pacific Dunlop. Page 27.

Beer and soft drink group Lion Nathan has appointed the head of its Pepsi-Cola subsidiary, Gordon Cairns, as managing director of its Australian operations, following the departure of Tony van Kralingen, who has returned to South Africa for family reasons. Cairns has been trying to turn the Pepsi operation around and was managing director of KFC South Pacific from 1993 to 1995. Page 27.

Addressing a major motor industry conference organised by the Society of Automotive Engineers Australasia, former Labor Government Minister John Button yesterday joined the call for a consumption tax to boost sales of new vehicles and said the Productivity Commission should "leave things very much as they are". Page 27.
THE AGE

After less than two months in the job, Lion Nathan's LNN.NZ. newly appointed managing director in Australia, Tony van Kralingen, has resigned. Lion will replace Kralingen with Gordon Cairns, who has been running the company's Pepsi franchise in Australia since March last year. Page B1.

Pacific Dunlop has sold its Telectronics pacemaker business to US-based St Jude Medical for A$170 million. The group had previously booked an expected loss of A$91 million on the sale of the Telectronics business as part of A$340 million in losses and provisions booked in the 1996 accounts against the business. Page B1.

Reflecting production problems at two of its gold mines and the impact of the low zinc price on the group's otherwise strongly performed base metals operation, Normandy Mining has posted a first quarter profit of A$20.5 million - a result executive chairman Robert Champion de Crespigny described as being below target. Page B1.
In an effort to raise funds before the end of the month, Australis Media has increased the bond yield on its A$190 million US bond issue from the 13.25 per cent set last week to a rich 15 per cent.

Mondex International, which owns the technology behind the Mondex stored-value card, will open up an office in Australia next year, with Melbourne the front-runner over Sydney as the favoured location. Visiting Melbourne yesterday, the group's chief exective officer Michael Keegan said Mondex was looking very seriously at moving its regional office from Hong Kong to Melbourne. Page B3.

Despite a 17 per cent increase in sales revenue from A$356 million to A$415 million, a surge in the cost of gold production and the impact of lower profit margins from copper sales have caused Placer Pacific's net profit for the nine months to September to drop to A$28.1 million from A$45.9 million. Page B3.
-- Reuters Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
